nodes.description: Lactose that reaches the colon is fermented by the resident microbiota into short-chain fatty acids and gas (hydrogen, carbon dioxide, methane). This is the arm that produces flatulence and much of the pain and distension, and the hydrogen it generates is what the breath test measures — so the principal diagnostic reads out this node rather than the enzymatic lesion itself.

nodes.description:
Lactase-phlorizin hydrolase at the enterocyte brush border, which hydrolyses lactose into glucose and galactose, falls in activity through childhood in non-persistent individuals. This is a physiological, developmentally timed decline rather than a disease process in the usual sense, and it is the default outcome for most of humanity. Reduced, not absent, activity is the key quantitative feature separating this from congenital lactase deficiency.
Deliberately carries no conforms_to. The diet_induced_osmotic_diarrhea trigger node describes a biallelic loss-of-function lesion and is annotated modifier: LOSS_OF_FUNCTION, where this node is a cis-regulatory downregulation annotated DECREASED. That is a difference in kind, not in degree, and the module's own trigger-node evidence names adult-type hypolactasia as not a conformer of it. Conformance is claimed only on the three downstream nodes, which the module describes as disorder-agnostic and which this disease genuinely shares.

nodes.description: Dietary lactose is an obligate exposure: the enzymatic lesion is present lifelong and silent, and every symptom in this entry is produced only when lactose is ingested. The relationship is dose-graded rather than all-or-nothing, because residual lactase handles small loads. This is the exposure that separates the trait from the syndrome, and it is why the principal treatment is a change in exposure rather than a drug.

evidence.reference_title: A comparison of symptoms after the consumption of milk or lactose-hydrolyzed milk by people with self-reported severe lactose intolerance.
evidence.snippet: When lactose intake is limited to the equivalent of 240 ml of milk or less a day, symptoms are likely to be negligible and the use of lactose-digestive aids unnecessary.

nodes.description:
Oral lactase enzyme taken with a lactose-containing meal, replacing the missing hydrolytic step so lactose is digested normally and never reaches the colon as fermentable substrate. Response is markedly variable rather than uniform: in 96 breath-test-positive, uniformly C/C-13910 patients given a standard oral beta-galactosidase dose, only about a fifth converted to a negative breath test and roughly 60% were essentially unchanged. The entry records that variability rather than presenting supplementation as reliably corrective.
therapeutic_agent is deliberately absent despite treatment_term being NCIT:C15986. The agent is the enzyme itself, and no candidate term is a member of the ChemicalEntityTerm enum, which is reachable only from CHEBI:24431 and NCIT:C1909 (Pharmacologic Substance): NCIT:C29147 Lactase sits under Dietary Supplement, NCIT:C107438 Beta-Galactosidase under Protein, and CHEBI has no term for the enzyme. Both CURIEs resolve, so this is an enum-membership gap rather than a missing term - do not re-add one without checking membership.

The causal variant is regulatory, not structural. Sequencing of the LCT coding and promoter regions found no variation tracking with the phenotype; instead a cis-acting element roughly 14 kb upstream, within an MCM6 intron, governs whether LCT transcription is maintained into adulthood. The ancestral C allele at C/T-13910 drives the enhancer weakly relative to the derived T allele, and reporter assays in intestinal cells show the two alleles differ in the transcriptional activation they confer and in the nuclear proteins they bind. Because this is a quantitative transcriptional effect rather than an inactivating lesion, residual lactase persists — which is why tolerance is dose-dependent rather than absolute.

nodes.description: Lactose retained in the small-bowel lumen is osmotically active, so water moves into the lumen down the osmotic gradient and the resulting volume distends the bowel. This is the arm that produces watery stool, and it is separated from the fermentative arm because the two have different consequences and respond differently to intervention: removing lactose removes both, but the gas-dominant complaints track fermentation specifically.

nodes.description: Lactose that is not hydrolysed cannot be absorbed, so it stays in the lumen as an osmotically active disaccharide. This is the rate-limiting, substrate-specific node shared with the other diet-induced osmotic diarrhoeas, and it is where dose-dependence enters: a small lactose load may be fully handled by residual enzyme, while a larger one saturates it.
